core_obligations: Reduce the lemma to the transitivity statement, the rest being clear from the construction of the rings (proof line 34618).
Assume there are two or more orbits and produce b in B_1 vanishing at all maximal ideals of one orbit and having residue 1 at all maximal ideals of another (proof lines 34619-34621).

Form b' = prod_{sigma in G} sigma(b) and observe that it is a G-invariant element of B_1 contained in L_1 = (L tensor_K K_1)_red which lies in some but not all maximal ideals of B_1 (proof lines 34622-34625).

In characteristic p > 0, lift b' to a G-invariant b'' in L tensor_K K_1 mapping to (b')^N for some N > 0, using that raising to a suitably large p-power q defines a canonical map (L tensor_K K_1)_red -> L tensor_K K_1 (proof lines 34626-34630).
Use K = (K_1)^G to conclude b'' lies in L, and that since b'' maps to an element of B_1 and B is normal it lies in B (proof lines 34631-34632).

Derive the contradiction: b'' must lie in the maximal ideal of B because b' lies in some maximal ideal of B_1, and must not lie in it because b' is not in all maximal ideals of B_1 (proof lines 34633-34637).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L, a normal extension K_1/K with automorphism group G, and asserts that G acts on the rings K_1, L_1, A_1 and B_1 and transitively on the maximal ideals of B_1 (source lines 34608-34615). The proof reduces immediately to the transitivity statement and argues by contradiction: if there are two or more orbits, one can find b in B_1 vanishing at all maximal ideals of one orbit and having residue 1 at all maximal ideals of another (proof lines 34618-34621). The substantive move is the construction of the G-invariant element b' = prod_{sigma in G} sigma(b), which lies in B_1 inside L_1 = (L tensor_K K_1)_red and lies in some but not all maximal ideals of B_1 (proof lines 34622-34625). The proof then has to lift b' back to L tensor_K K_1: in characteristic p > 0 it raises to a suitably large p-power q, which defines a canonical map (L tensor_K K_1)_red -> L tensor_K K_1, obtaining a G-invariant b'' mapping to (b')^N (proof lines 34626-34630). Since K = (K_1)^G one gets b'' in L, and since b'' maps to B_1 and B is normal one gets b'' in B; but then b'' must lie in the maximal ideal of B because b' lies in some maximal ideal of B_1, and simultaneously must not, because b' does not lie in all of them, a contradiction (proof lines 34631-34637). The non-routine step is the characteristic p lifting of a reduced-tensor element through a p-power Frobenius-type map.
